subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 17-year-old boy is evaluated for decreased vision and pain in his legs. He is tall with long limbs, and his upper-to-lower body segment ratio is reduced. Slit-lamp examination shows downward and inward displacement of both lenses, and he has pectus excavatum and kyphosis. He has mild intellectual disability and was recently treated for a deep venous thrombosis. Plasma homocysteine is markedly elevated and plasma methionine is also elevated, while methylmalonic acid is normal.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is the most likely cause of this presentation?
explanation_correct: Cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency is the most common cause of homocystinuria and blocks the transsulfuration of homocysteine to cystathionine, so homocysteine and its precursor methionine both accumulate. It produces the classic triad of Marfanoid habitus, downward and inward (nasal) lens subluxation, and thrombotic events, along with osteoporosis and intellectual disability. Treatment includes a methionine-restricted diet, cysteine supplementation, and pyridoxine, B12, and folate.

explanation_incorrect.A: Methionine synthase deficiency also raises homocysteine, but methionine is typically low rather than elevated, and the classic Marfanoid skeletal and ocular phenotype is not typical.
explanation_incorrect.B: Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase deficiency limits remethylation of homocysteine and produces hyperhomocysteinemia with normal or low methionine; the classic Marfanoid skeletal and lens phenotype is less characteristic.
explanation_incorrect.D: Methionine adenosyltransferase deficiency causes isolated hypermethioninemia without marked hyperhomocysteinemia, lens subluxation, or thrombosis.
explanation_incorrect.E: Homogentisate oxidase deficiency causes alkaptonuria with dark urine, ochronosis, and arthropathy, not homocystinuria.

educationalObjective: Cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency is the most common cause of homocystinuria and produces marked elevations of homocysteine and methionine together with Marfanoid features, downward lens subluxation, and thrombosis.
